neighbours.label: the one member singled out against a group: the exception or lone individual after 'all / the others ... but' (except [one], but not [me], but this [time]); the - pole takes the group side (many of, most of, all)
fire: Every window in the house was dark, except one.
The others all found the film hilarious, but not me.
She had turned the offer down three times already, but this time she said yes.
All the soldiers ran from the dragon. At last a young shepherd stepped forward.
The whole class handed in the essay on Friday, all but one.
Critics hated the play, and so did the audience, but not her.
Forty-nine letters went unanswered, but he got lucky with the fiftieth.
Each of the brothers refused to help the old woman, except the youngest.
quiet: Every window in the house was dark and the doors were locked.
The others all found the film hilarious and laughed until the end.
She had turned the offer down three times already and saw no reason to change.
All the soldiers ran from the dragon. Many of them dropped their shields.
The whole class handed in the essay on Friday, as most of them usually do.
Critics hated the play, and so did the audience on opening night.
Forty-nine letters went unanswered, and many of them were never opened.
Each of the brothers refused to help the old woman carry her wood.

notes: Probe: 'but not me' 1.51, 'except one' 0.54, 'Then a stable boy came along' 0.36, 'but this time' 0.35; 'most of them left' 0.01.
